model: Underlying profit capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: terminal_growth for the capitalised underlying-profit stream; the explicit years follow the disclosed handover pipeline (FY2027-28 bulge, then normalisation) rather than any historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1%) diverges from revenue CAGR (+10% 3yr) by far more than 30%: revenue growth is handover timing (FY2024-25 HK deliveries) while book value has been eroded by HK$4.4bn of cumulative investment-property fair-value losses FY2022-25 and dividends paid above earnings. EPS CAGRs (-30%) are statutory and revaluation-dominated; the meaningful series is underlying profit (fcf_* rows above): FY2020 ~4,200 -> FY2021 6,266 -> FY2022 4,520 (3,235 ex Kerry Logistics disposal gain) -> FY2023 2,518 -> FY2024 2,576 (3,973 ex provisions) -> FY2025 2,008 (2,455 ex provisions). Statutory revenue (subsidiaries only): FY2020 14,526 -> FY2022 14,591 -> FY2025 19,568. Equity: FY2020 109,873 -> FY2022 108,787 -> FY2025 105,272. EPS: 3.71 -> 1.90 -> 0.65.
historical_growth.notes: The fcf_* CAGRs are computed on the underlying-profit series (the flow this model capitalises), not on reported FCF, whose sign flips with the inventory cycle. FY2025 UNP is at or near a cyclical trough: office rents down, HK$447m of development provisions, finance costs up as capitalised interest fell after the Jinling launch. The 10-year UNP range is roughly HK$2.0-6.3bn; the base case normalises to ~HK$2.8-3.1bn in the out-years, below the decade mid-point.

scenario_narratives.base: The visible pipeline plays out roughly on schedule. HK$29.8bn of presold stock (HK$23.9bn Shanghai Jinling Residences at record per-sq-m prices, HK$5.9bn Hong Kong led by Mont Verra) is handed over and booked across FY2026-FY2028, lifting underlying profit from a FY2025 trough of HK$2.0bn to a FY2028 peak near HK$3.7bn, then fading to ~HK$2.8bn by FY2030 as the Jinling tail runs off while the Huangpu mixed-use project, the three new HK sites and the Shanghai Pudong site are still being built. Rental income is flat-to-down: Mainland office oversupply (Shanghai Grade-A vacancy >20%) erodes Kerry Centre rents at roughly the pace that the HK apartment-for-lease book and new IP completions add. Gearing keeps falling with sales proceeds and the HK$1.35 dividend is held. Out-year growth 2%, terminal 1.5%, exit capped at 12x UNP.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Hong Kong residential cycle that was inflecting in 1H2026 (land prices +40% YoY, inventory months at a 3-year low, Mainland wealth inflows) carries through to the new HK sites at full margins; Jinling's remaining phases keep selling out at record prices with no further provisions; Mainland office rents find a floor in 2027 as supply additions slow; the Huangpu MUD commercial portion opens 2029-2031 and adds a second Jing An Kerry Centre-scale rental stream; HKD rates fall and the 3.5% effective interest rate drifts toward 3%. Underlying profit peaks near HK$4.6bn in FY2028 and settles around HK$3.7bn, growing 3% as the 6.5m sq ft IP pipeline fills. Terminal growth 2%, exit 14x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Jinling handovers slip and the net take is squeezed by land appreciation tax and another HK$1bn-plus of Mainland provisions; sales outside Shanghai remain 'disappointingly slow', so there is no second project to replace Jinling after FY2028; Shanghai and Shenzhen office vacancy of 20-30% forces rent cuts across the Kerry Centres and HK office and retail stay soft; RMB weakness translates into lower HKD earnings. Underlying profit recovers only to ~HK$2.5bn at the FY2028 peak and settles below HK$2bn, so the HK$1.35 dividend is uncovered and eventually cut; the market re-rates the stock toward 9x a smaller earnings base. The balance sheet survives (gearing ~30%, 2.4-year average debt maturity refinanced at the Kuok Group's banking relationships), so this is an earnings-and-multiple bear, not a solvency bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kerry Properties is valued as a stream of underlying profit (the company's audited measure of attributable earnings excluding investment-property revaluations) capitalised at a 10% HKD cost of equity, with net debt held at zero because the flow is already post-interest. The explicit ten years follow the disclosed handover pipeline -- a FY2027-28 bulge from HK$29.8bn of presold stock, then normalisation -- rather than a smooth growth rate, and the terminal multiple is capped at 9-14x underlying profit depending on scenario. The result should be read against the stock's decade-long 0.22-0.55x price-to-book range and against the HK$1.35 dividend (a ~7.5% yield at the current price, ~100% of FY2025 underlying profit): the model pays for earnings and dividends, not for the HK$72.5 of stated NAV per share, which HK developer shareholders have never been able to realise.
key_risks_to_valuation: Timing and net margin of the Jinling Residences handovers (HK$23.9bn unrecognised): a one-year slip or a heavier land-appreciation-tax bill moves the FY2027-28 peak and ~HK$2-3/share of value
Mainland Grade-A office rents: the largest recurring-income segment, with Shanghai vacancy above 20% and Shenzhen near 30%; a further 10% rent decline is roughly HK$0.3bn of UNP
Further development-property provisions (HK$447m FY2025, HK$1,397m FY2024) on the second- and third-tier Mainland pipeline
Refinancing: HK$55bn of borrowings with a ~2.4-2.5 year average maturity; the model assumes the Kuok Group banking relationships roll it at ~3.5%
RMB/HKD translation: most assets and revenue are RMB while the HKD is pegged to the USD
Capital allocation: three HK sites and a Shanghai Pudong site bought in 2026 at a rising-land-price moment; returns on this ~HK$10bn+ of new land are not in the explicit years
Cost of equity: at a 10% rate a 100bp move is worth roughly HK$2.5-3.0/share on the base case; HK rates track US rates through the peg

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (0683.HK, HKD), regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 17.07-26.10
data_sources.financials: 0683.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (HKD millions, FY2017-FY2025 annuals plus H1 FY2023-FY2026 interims); FY2025 Annual Report (underlying profit bridge lines 330-360, segment revenue 65-72, NAV/share 85, gearing 97, Jinling status 1261-1292, unrecognised sales 466) and 1H2026 Interim Report (UNP 217-221, unrecognised sales 347-352, net debt and total equity 998-999, shares 2156/2978, effective interest rate 320)
data_sources.qualitative: 0683.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-11): business model, Jinling concentration, Mainland office oversupply, HK cycle inflection, deleveraging path, broker targets HK$22.70 (HSBC) and HK$25.55 (Citi)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 Underlying Profit (profit attributable to shareholders excluding non-cash fair-value changes of investment properties, net of deferred tax), 0683.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:344. This is the capitalised stream, fed through the engine's revenue line at 100% margin with D&A, capex, SBC and tax paths set to zero because UNP is already attributable, post-interest and post-tax.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,446,480,329 ordinary shares outstanding at 30 June 2026 (1,451,305,728 in issue less ~4.8m shares held by the Share Award Scheme trust), 0683.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:2156 and :2978. No options or convertibles; diluted = basic. Held flat: SBC is immaterial (HK$19m FY2025) and is already expensed inside underlying profit.
inputs.net_debt_note: Underlying profit is a post-interest equity flow capitalised at the cost of equity, so net debt is deliberately NOT deducted again (deducting it would charge the HK$37.8bn twice). Actual 30 June 2026 net debt HK$37,826m = borrowings 55,217 - cash and bank deposits 17,391; gearing (net debt / total equity 120,883) 31.3%, down from 41.5% at FY2024. Recorded in total_debt / cash for audit.
inputs.last_fcf_note: On this route last_fcf is FY2025 Underlying Profit, not owner FCF. Reported FCF (OCF less payments for investment properties/PP&E) is an inventory cycle for a developer: HK$12,560m in FY2025 and HK$5,639m in 1H2025 as completed stock was sold down, -HK$780m in FY2022 while land was bought. It is not a repeatable base and is not capitalised.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement share award expense HK$19m (1H2026: HK$12m); Share Award Scheme capped at 10% of shares, grants at 1%. Immaterial and already inside underlying profit, so the forward SBC path is 0%.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest received HK$497m stays inside underlying profit and the cash that earns it stays out of the bridge (matching-asset rule, both sides consistent). Cash is operating liquidity for a 31%-geared developer, not surplus.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, HKD-denominated flows: HKD 10-year government bond ~3.5% (HKD is USD-pegged, HK rates track UST) + 6.0% equity risk premium blended for a HK-listed company with ~75-80% of GFA on the Chinese Mainland x beta ~1.1 for a geared HK/China property developer-investor = ~10.1%, rounded to 10.0%. Applied to an already-levered, post-interest flow, so no debt cost enters. Same rate in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the flows and the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates. Wharf (0004.HK), the folder's nearest comparable, uses 9.5% on a net-cash balance sheet; Kerry's 31% gearing and heavier Mainland mix justify 50bp more.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities HK$25m at FY2025 (HK$53m undiscounted) and lease principal payments HK$45m/yr are immaterial and are already charged inside underlying profit (depreciation and interest on ROU assets). No separate deduction; nothing in net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Underlying profit is attributable to shareholders of the Company, so the HK$13.9bn of non-controlling interests (FY2025) is already excluded from the flow. No NCI deduction in the bridge (charging it once). This NCI balance is also what explains the identity_balance eval warning on FY2017-2022: TotalAssets - TotalLiabilities - ShareholdersEquity = 13,362 (FY2017) and exactly 13,900 (FY2023), i.e. the NCI line that core_metrics' ShareholdersEquity excludes.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Underlying Profit (company's audited non-GAAP distributable-earnings measure, N3 in the annual report) capitalised at a 10% HKD cost of equity, net_debt=0, on the Drivers/engine route -- the same family as Wharf (0004.HK), Charter Hall, Goodman and IAG.AX. WHY NOT OWNER-FCF: statutory profit and reported FCF are unusable anchors for a mixed developer/investor -- statutory profit carries IAS 40 fair-value swings (FY2021 inflated by gains, FY2024-25 depressed by HK$1.8bn/HK$1.1bn of losses) and reported FCF is a land-and-inventory cycle (-HK$0.8bn FY2022 to +HK$12.6bn FY2025). WHY NOT NAV: the company's NAV/share is HK$72.54 (FY2025) and HK$73.7 on 1H2026 attributable equity, but the stock has traded at 0.22-0.55x book for a decade; a NAV model would need a 60-70% discount with no earnings discipline behind it. The UNP route values what shareholders actually receive and produces an implied P/B that can be checked against that history (0.22-0.55x; 52-week 0.23-0.36x). UNP spans all three segments: property sales 71% / rental and others 21% / hotels 8% of FY2025 combined revenue (incl. JVs and associates). SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position is null by construction. Anchors: price regular close 2026-10-09; balance sheet and share count at 30 June 2026 interim; FY2026 'guidance' is non-numeric -- the company discloses HK$29.8bn of contracted sales yet to be recognised (HK$23.9bn Mainland, chiefly Shanghai Jinling Residences handing over in phases from 2026; HK$5.9bn Hong Kong, chiefly Mont Verra), 1H2026 UNP HK$782m (-9%), interim DPS HK$0.40 maintained, gearing 31.3% and falling, effective interest rate 3.5%.

bear.growth_note: UNP HK$m: 1,707 -> 2,202 -> 2,510 -> 2,108 -> 1,898 -> +1%/yr. Jinling handovers slip into 2028 and land appreciation tax plus further Mainland provisions (HK$1.4bn FY2024-25 run-rate continues) compress the net take; Mainland sales outside Shanghai stay 'disappointingly slow' so the post-Jinling pipeline is thin; Shanghai/Shenzhen office vacancy at 20-30% forces rent cuts at the Kerry Centres; HK office/retail stays soft; RMB weakens against the pegged HKD. UNP never regains the FY2023-24 level and the HK$1.35 dividend is uncovered until FY2027.

base.growth_note: UNP path HK$m: FY2025 2,008 -> FY2026 1,908 (1H 782, -9%; H2 similar with Mont Verra/LA MIRABELLE handovers but softer office rents and lower interest capitalisation) -> FY2027 3,052 (first Jinling Residences handovers; ~HK$8-10bn of Mainland revenue at ~40% gross margin less land appreciation tax and 25% CIT) -> FY2028 3,663 (peak Jinling bookings) -> FY2029 3,113 -> FY2030 2,802 as the Jinling tail fades and Huangpu MUD / HK sites are still under construction, then +2%/yr: the ~6.5m sq ft of new IP/hotel GFA through ~2033 (Shanghai Huangpu MUD, Wuhan, Shenyang) offsets gradual Mainland office rent erosion.
base.terminal_note: Cap 12x underlying profit: HK developers/investors have traded at ~8-14x underlying earnings through the cycle; 12x is the ceiling a buyer plausibly pays for a 31%-geared, Mainland-heavy book. Terminal growth 1.5% below HK/China nominal growth reflects structural Mainland office oversupply offsetting the new-IP pipeline.

bull.growth_note: UNP HK$m: 2,108 -> 3,816 -> 4,617 -> 4,017 -> 3,716 -> +3%/yr. HK residential recovery (land prices +40% YoY in 1H2026, inventory at a 3-year low) lifts HK development margins; Jinling later phases sell at record Shanghai prices with no further provisions; Mainland office rents stabilise in 2027; Huangpu MUD commercial opens 2029-31 and adds a Jing An Kerry Centre-scale rental stream; lower HKD rates cut finance costs toward 3%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default because the Mainland sales recovery rests on a single project (Jinling Residences) and the largest investment-property segment (Mainland office) faces structural, not cyclical, oversupply; two independent weak markets, a 2.4-year debt maturity and RMB translation risk all sit on the downside. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: a sustained HK residential upcycle, a Mainland office floor and on-time Huangpu MUD delivery. Base 50%: the FY2027-28 earnings bulge is largely contracted and paid for, which is why the base is not weighted lower.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
